aspects.says: Field 7 is the transmission time in GMT, whatever the zone of the server or of the clock.
basis: section:2.4 Field 7 Is GMT, Whatever the Server's Time Zone

aspects.says: Masking is applied to what is printed or logged; the message keeps the real PAN, and dump prints it in clear.
basis: section:2.6 Mask What You Print, Never What You Send

aspects.says: A message that does not pack fails on the channel thread: the caller sees only a timeout and the 2.1.7 adaptor drops the link, so pack with the link's packager before queueing and report such a message as not sent.
basis: section:2.2 A Message That Doesn't Pack Fails on the Channel Thread

aspects.says: The fields every message on a link carries are set in one method of a factory with an injected clock and counter, so every message type gets them alike.
basis: section:2.3 The Fields Every Request Shares Are Set in One Place

aspects.says: The STAN is one counting sequence per link, shared by every message type, from 000001 to 999999 and around again; random and time-of-day STANs collide.
basis: section:2.5 The STAN Is One Sequence per Link

aspects.says: An ISOMsg keeps the strings it was given; the packager pads short values and refuses long ones only when it packs, so a short STAN in memory differs from the one the host echoes.
basis: section:2.1 An ISOMsg Holds Strings, and the Packager Decides the Bytes
